## 2. Hierarchy body — every syllabus sub-point
### Microbes as biocontrol agents and biofertilizers

Fill order per concept: definition → structure → process → significance (§3.2). Step-by-step numbered points, Pioneer style.

Chemical pesticides and fertilisers pollute and cost energy. The biological alternative uses living microbes: **biocontrol agents** are microbes (or their predators) that kill pests and weeds; **biofertilizers** are microbes that supply plant nutrients, chiefly by fixing atmospheric nitrogen. Both are the backbone of organic farming.

**Concept flow — from chemical dependence to biological control (study in this order)**

| Step | Concept | Example |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The problem with chemicals | Residues, resistance, killing of non-target insects, eutrophication from fertiliser runoff |
| 2 | Biocontrol with bacteria | Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) toxin kills caterpillars; gene now used in Bt cotton |
| 3 | Biocontrol with fungi and viruses | Trichoderma against soil fungi; baculovirus (NPV) against insect larvae |
| 4 | Biocontrol with predator insects | Ladybird beetle eats aphids; dragonflies eat mosquitoes |
| 5 | Biofertilizers — symbiotic N fixers | Rhizobium in legume root nodules; Azolla-Anabaena in rice paddies |
| 6 | Biofertilizers — free-living and fungal | Azotobacter, Azospirillum; mycorrhiza (Glomus) improves water and phosphorus uptake |

**Biocontrol agents — who kills what**

| Agent | Type | Target pest | How it works |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) | Soil bacterium | Caterpillars, beetle larvae, fly larvae | Produces Bt toxin crystals; alkaline insect gut dissolves them, toxin kills gut cells |
| Bt cotton (transgenic) | Crop carrying the Bt gene | Bollworm | Plant itself produces the toxin |
| Trichoderma viride | Fungus | Root-rot and wilt fungi | Antagonistic — parasitises and outcompetes pathogenic fungi |
| Baculovirus (NPV) | Insect virus | Lepidopteran larvae (moth, butterfly caterpillars) | Infects and liquefies larvae; harmless to plants, birds, mammals |
| Ladybird beetle | Predatory insect | Aphids (plant lice) | Eats large numbers of aphids |
| Dragonflies | Predatory insect | Mosquitoes | Eats mosquito larvae and adults |

**Biofertilizers — classified by how they fix or supply nutrients**

| Biofertilizer | Type | Host / habitat | What it supplies |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rhizobium | Symbiotic bacterium | Root nodules of legumes (pea, beans, pulses) | Fixed atmospheric nitrogen to the plant |
| Frankia | Symbiotic actinomycete | Root nodules of Alnus (alder) | Nitrogen fixation in non-legumes |
| Azolla + Anabaena | Symbiosis: fern + cyanobacterium | Rice paddies | Anabaena fixes nitrogen in Azolla leaf cavities — green manure for rice |
| Azotobacter / Azospirillum | Free-living aerobic bacteria | Soil around roots (rhizosphere) | Fix nitrogen without a host |
| Glomus (mycorrhiza) | Symbiotic fungus | Roots of most plants | Huge surface area: better phosphorus and water uptake, disease resistance |

## 6. Key terms and statements
Every new term defined once; exam-grade definitions live here and in keyPoints (block VI).

**Worked example — why Bt cotton works.** The caterpillar bites the leaf; the plant's own cells now carry the *cry* gene from *Bacillus thuringiensis* and produce an inactive protoxin. The insect's alkaline gut juice dissolves it, the toxin is activated, gut cells rupture and the larva dies within days. Humans and birds have acidic guts — the toxin is inactive for us. One gene moved the pesticide from the spray can into the plant.

## 8. Summary and self-check
5–10 line chapter summary, self-check questions and the common-confusions list (block VIII) — completed in the unit fill pass.

**Summary.** Biocontrol replaces poison with predators, pathogens and toxins aimed at pests; biofertilizers replace bagged fertiliser with nitrogen-fixing and phosphorus-scavenging microbes. Both are specific, self-renewing and residue-free. **Self-check:** can you place each agent in the right column — bacteria, fungus, virus, predator, symbiont?

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Biocontrol bank: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt toxin kills insect larvae — Bt cotton carries the gene), Trichoderma (fungus vs plant pathogens), ladybird/Aphatelina beetles vs aphids, Baculovirus (insect-specific, harmless to plants/birds/fish).
Trick 2: Merit line: biocontrol is target-specific, no chemical residue, no resistance build-up — the eco advantage over pesticides.
Trick 3: Biofertilizers: Rhizobium, Azospirillum, cyanobacteria, mycorrhiza — reuse of the earlier list with the biocontrol contrast.
Trick 4: Bt toxin detail: inactive protoxin → activated in insect gut (alkaline pH) → binds midgut cells → lysis — the activation mechanism is the 2-marker.
